The major streams of the area and their many intermittent tributaries erode the land surface of the tracts and transport sediment from the drainage basins of the Project Area.
In analyzing unpublished data compiled by the U.S. Dept. of Agriculture, Soil Conservation Service, for the Wind, Bighorn, and Clarks

Fork River basins, the U.S. Bureau of Indian Affairs (1974, p. 81)

Dryland agriculture, which occurs to a limited extent on the relatively flat areas of the plateaus of Tracts II and III, is estimated to have a base sediment yield ranging from 0.4 to 1.0 AF/SM/YR.
Sediment yield from a given drainage basin is dependent upon such factors as: geology of the area, nature of the soils, vegetative cover, topography, climate and local meteorology, amount and frequency of runoff, and use of the land. Sediment yields from the drainages of Tracts II and III have not been measured.
